text:
maria: Quick note — after the fused-attn kernel switch p95 for short streaming responses climbed. Observed with default chunk flush 40ms.

aditya: saw that in the dashboard. Any profile snapshots yet?

perf-bot: canary-profile uploaded: https://perf.internal/reports/1987 -> flame + timeline

maria: flame looks like wait time sits between token arrival and kernel dispatch, especially for microbatch sizes of 4. KV hits are high though.

sam: my hunch: interaction between microbatch boundaries and the chunk flush timer. If we hold chunk flush at 40ms, short responses wait for the next flush even if KV would allow earlier emit.

jia: we should try lowering flush interval to see perceived latency effect. 40ms -> 12ms as an A/B. That will increase kernel calls but should reduce tail.

natalie: tradeoff reminder: smaller emit quantum reduces p95 but increases kernel launch overhead and hurts peak throughput. Need numbers.

aditya: can we also tag traces with kernel_type=(fused|fallback) and kv_hit_rate so we can slice perf by those dimensions?

maria: ran quick canary: chunk=12ms -> p95 down from ~330ms -> ~210ms for 1-3 token responses on rtx-like nodes. Peak throughput dropped ~8%. p99 improved slightly.

sam: that suggests queueing from flush interval is a big contributor. Kernel choice still a factor at seq>128 though.

jia: pushed a small adaptive flush patch: if KV hit and pending_tokens < emit_threshold we flush immediately, else schedule normal interval. Rough snippet: 
```
// adaptive flush
if (kv_hit && pending_tokens < emit_threshold) {
  flush_now();
} else {
  schedule_flush(interval_ms);
}
```

natalie: I like adaptive. Also add a cap on microbatch size to avoid forming huge batches when using small intervals. Maybe batch_cap=8 for adaptive runs.

aditya: added telemetry fields: emit_quantum_ms, kernel_launch_ms, batch_size_observed. Dashboard updated to show p95/p99 per kernel_type and per-emit_quantum bucket.

perf-bot: adaptive-flush canary results: p95 improved by 95ms avg vs baseline 40ms. Throughput delta -6.5% at peak. Full logs: https://perf.internal/logs/1987-adaptive

maria: interesting — adaptive mostly recovers tail without as much throughput loss as fixed small quantum. Means we get best of both worlds for interactive short responses.

sam: watch out for microburst of kernel launches when many clients emit simultaneously. Small quanta can create short-lived bursts of kernel_start overhead. We should simulate spike scenario and measure kernel_launch_ms distribution.

jia: added spike test to perf harness (burst 500 concurrent short chats). Preliminary: fixed 12ms quantum -> peak kernel_launch_ms up 1.8x; adaptive -> more moderate increase.

aditya: proposal for rollout: canary adaptive in prod with guard: rollback if throughput drop >10% or avg kernel_launch_ms > 2x baseline for >5min. Also add automatic fallback to 40ms fixed for Dedicated customers on high throughput plans.

maria: opening rollout PR with documentation of tradeoffs and the telemetry knobs. Will include recommended defaults per deployment class (hosted: adaptive default, dedicated-high-throughput: 40ms default).

natalie: :thumbsup: Also add note in Optimize docs about tuning emit_quantum vs batch_cap vs kernel selection for workload shapes.

aditya: one more ask — collect per-token perceived-latency metric (time from client-first-byte to first-emitted-token) so product can quantify UX improvement.

perf-bot: canary complete. Summaries: adaptive emits reduce perceived p95 by ~100ms on chat-like flows, throughput cost ~6-9% depending on node type. Revert policy and dashboards in place.

maria: thanks — will follow up with PR and a short runbook for oncall if we see regression after rollout.
